writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 170 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
There is a growing awareness of the importance of digital literacy and skills in today’s world. As study, work and daily life move online, the ability to use digital tools wisely has become a basic survival skill rather than an optional advantage.
This importance is easy to feel in real situations. During the pandemic, all my courses were shifted to online platforms, and only classmates who could navigate video meetings, submit assignments and search for reliable sources kept up with the pace. Those who struggled with the technology quickly fell behind, not because they were less clever, but because they lacked the digital skills the new setting demanded. The same gap appears in the job market, where employers now expect graduates to handle data, communicate online and tell trustworthy information from rumours.
Therefore, digital literacy is no longer a bonus but a necessity. By actively learning to process information, protect our online safety and keep updating our skills, we can turn technology into a real advantage instead of a barrier.

cloze.title: 2024年6月·第3套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: A rainbow is a multi-colored, arc-shaped phenomenon that can appear in the sky. The colors of a rainbow are produced by the reflection and __(26)__ of light through water droplets(小滴) present in the atmosphere. An observer may __(27)__ a rainbow to be located either near or far away, but this phenomenon is not actually located at any specific spot. Instead, the appearance of a rainbow depends entirely upon the position of the observer in __(28)__ to the direction of light. In essence, a rainbow is an __(29)__ illusion.
passages.zh: 彩虹是一种可能出现在天空中的多色弧形现象。彩虹的颜色是由大气中水滴对光线的反射和色散产生的。观察者可能会觉得彩虹位于近处或远处，但这种现象实际上并不位于任何特定地点。相反，彩虹的出现完全取决于观察者相对于光线方向所处的位置。从本质上说，彩虹是一种视觉错觉。

passages.en: Rainbows present a __(30)__ made up of seven colors in a specific order. In fact, school children in many English-speaking countries are taught to remember the name "Roy G. Biv" as an aid for remembering the colors of a rainbow and their order. "Roy G. Biv" __(31)__ for: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. The outer edge of the rainbow arc is red, while the inner edge is violet.
passages.zh: 彩虹呈现出由七种颜色按特定顺序组成的光谱。事实上，许多英语国家的学校会教孩子们记住“Roy G. Biv”这个名字，以帮助他们记忆彩虹的颜色及其顺序。“Roy G. Biv”分别代表：红色、橙色、黄色、绿色、蓝色、靛蓝色和紫色。彩虹弧的外缘是红色，内缘是紫色。

passages.en: A rainbow is formed when light (generally sunlight) passes through water droplets __(32)__ in the atmosphere. The light waves change direction as they pass through the water droplets, resulting in two processes: reflection and refraction(折射). When light reflects off a water droplet, it simply __(33)__ back in the opposite direction from where it __(34)__ . When light refracts, it takes a different direction. Some individuals refer to refracted light as "bent light waves." A rainbow is formed because white light enters the water droplet, where it bends in several different directions. When these bent light waves reach the other side of the water droplet, they reflect back out of the droplet instead of __(35)__ passing through the water. Since the white light is separated inside of the water, the refracted light appears as separate colors to the human eye.
passages.zh: 当光线（通常是阳光）穿过悬浮在大气中的水滴时，就会形成彩虹。光波穿过水滴时会改变方向，从而产生两个过程：反射和折射。当光线从水滴上反射回来时，它会沿着与光线来源相反的方向简单地弹回。当光线发生折射时，它会转向另一个方向。有些人把折射光称为“弯曲的光波”。彩虹之所以形成，是因为白光进入水滴后，会向几个不同的方向弯曲。当这些弯曲的光波到达水滴的另一侧时，它们会从水滴中反射出来，而不是完全穿过水滴。由于白光在水中发生了分离，折射光在人眼中就呈现为不同的颜色。

wordbank.gloss: 悬挂的；悬浮的（现在分词作定语）
起源、发源（不及物，常接 from/in）
关系；in relation to 关于、相对于

rows.text: C) dispersion名词
and 并列连接：reflection and ___，并列成分要求同性

reflection and dispersion 是描述彩虹成因的标准搭配 The colors of a rainbow are produced by the reflection and dispersion of light through water droplets 光经过水滴时发生「反射 + 色散」是彩虹七色形成的物理原理；与下一段 reflection and refraction（折射）共同呼应「光在水滴中的多重作用」。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— spectrum 也是名词，且与彩虹七色话题强相关，极易抢答 26。produced by the reflection and __(26)__ of light through water droplets 26 题若考生没等到 30 题就抢着填，看到「彩虹 + 光」很容易顺手填 N spectrum；但 26 题靠 and 并列须填与 reflection 同类的「光学过程」名词（dispersion 色散），spectrum「光谱」属结果性名词，且 spectrum 真正归属 30 题 a ___ made up of seven colors。防坑：严格执行「用过即划 + 先做高把握空」，让 30 题先把 spectrum 划走。
H) perceive动词
情态动词 may 后接动词原形

perceive sb/sth to be ... 「察觉/认为……是……」 An observer may perceive a rainbow to be located either near or far away perceive 后可直接接「宾语 + to be + 状态」，意为「察觉/认为彩虹位于近处或远处」，与下句 but this phenomenon is not actually located at any specific spot 形成「主观感知 vs 客观事实」的转折。
J)ponderponder 表「沉思」，不接「宾语 + to be」 ponder 通常作不及物或接 sth/on sth/over sth，不构成「ponder sth to be ...」结构；语义上「观察者沉思彩虹位于近处或远处」也极不自然。
M) relation名词
介词 in 后 + to 之前，构成 in ___ to 框架

固定短语 in relation to = 「相对于、关于」 the appearance of a rainbow depends entirely upon the position of the observer in __(28)__ to the direction of light. 文意是「彩虹出现完全取决于观察者相对于光线方向的位置」，正是 in relation to 的典型用法。
C)dispersion无 in dispersion to 这一搭配 dispersion 表「色散」，与「位置 ↔ 光线方向」的相对关系无关，且不构成固定短语 in dispersion to。 N)spectrumspectrum 指「光谱/范围」，搭配错误 spectrum 是后文 30 题对应「七色光谱」的名词，与「相对位置」语义不沾边，且无 in spectrum to 短语。
F) optical形容词
不定冠词 an + 空 + 名词 illusion
optical illusion = 「视错觉、光学幻象」固定搭配 In essence, a rainbow is an optical illusion. 上文已经指出彩虹「并非真实位于某一地点，而是取决于观察者的相对位置」，结论自然是「光学幻象」——optical illusion 是英语中表「视错觉」的标准搭配，与全段论证完全吻合。
D)eccentriceccentric 表「古怪的」，色彩与语境不符 eccentric 多形容人/行为「古怪、反常」，描述彩虹这一自然光学现象时既不准确也不带这种语义色彩；eccentric illusion 并非英语习用搭配。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 D) —— eccentric 形态匹配 an + 形容词 + illusion，最容易抢 29。a rainbow is an __(29)__ illusion. eccentric 以元音 /ɪ/ 开头与 an 适配、作前置定语语法完全通；但 optical illusion 才是英语固定搭配「视错觉」，本段全段都在论证「彩虹是观察者视觉上的幻象」，与「光学」直接对应。防坑：见 illusion 先想 optical illusion 这一高频固定搭配，再回头比对其它候选。
N) spectrum名词
及物动词 present 后 + 不定冠词 a 后
spectrum = 「光谱」，正对应「七色按特定顺序」 Rainbows present a spectrum made up of seven colors in a specific order. 「由七种颜色按特定顺序组成」正是 spectrum（光谱）的定义；下文 Roy G. Biv 口诀也是为了记忆这一光谱顺序。
C)dispersiondispersion 强调「色散过程」，非结果性的「七色排列」 dispersion 指光被分解的「过程/动作」，而本句 made up of seven colors in a specific order 描述的是一个由七色组成的「结果性序列」——这是 spectrum 的语义，不是 dispersion 的语义；且 dispersion 已被 26 题预订（见后）。
O) stands动词
主语 "Roy G. Biv" 后缺谓语 + 后接 for

固定搭配 stand for = 「代表、缩写指代」 "Roy G. Biv" __(31)__ for: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. 紧随其后的就是七色英文首字母对应的全称，文意正是「Roy G. Biv 这一串字母代表红橙黄绿蓝靛紫」，stand for 是固定搭配，意为「代表 / 是……的缩写」，与语境完全契合。

G)originatesoriginate 后不接 for originate 表「起源于」，常搭 originate from/in，无 originate for 这一搭配；语义也讲不通——「Roy G. Biv 起源于红橙黄……」不成立。 H)perceive形态不符 + 搭配不通 perceive 非单三，且 perceive for 不是固定搭配；它的宾语应是被感知的对象（如本文 27 题用法），与此处「代表七色」不符。 I)permeatespermeate 意为「渗透」 permeate 表液体/气味/影响渗透弥漫，搭配介词通常是 through/into，与「字母代表颜色」毫不相干。 J)ponder形态不符 + 语义不通 ponder 非单三；其义为「沉思」，主语「Roy G. Biv」是个口诀，不会「沉思」，逻辑不成立。
E) hanging形容词
名词 water droplets 后置修饰 + 空后接 in the atmosphere 介词短语
hanging in the atmosphere = 「悬浮在大气中」 water droplets hanging in the atmosphere 与第 1 段 water droplets(小滴) present in the atmosphere 同义改写，hanging 形象描绘水滴「悬浮 / 飘在」空中的状态，与上下文「光穿过水滴形成彩虹」语境完全一致。
K)precedingpreceding 表「在前的、先前的」，语义与空间状态无关 preceding 多用于时间或顺序「前一个、之前的」（如 in the preceding paragraph），不能用来描述水滴「悬浮在大气中」的物理状态。
A) bounces动词
主语 it（= 光）后缺谓语，且与并列分句时态一致

bounce back = 「反弹回去」，与 reflect 同义改写 When light reflects off a water droplet, it simply bounces back in the opposite direction from where it __(34)__. 上文 reflects 已给出动作，本句用 simply bounces back 同义改写以「反弹回来」的形象语言再说一遍，与 in the opposite direction 表方向反向严丝合缝。

G)originatesoriginate 表「起源」，与「反弹回来」语义相反 originate 强调「光从某处发源」，与本句 reflect / back / opposite direction 的「返回」语义方向相反，不可选。 I)permeatespermeate 是「渗透、弥漫」，与 bounce back 行为完全相反 permeate 表向内/向四周扩散，与「沿反方向反弹回去」（in the opposite direction）的物理路径冲突。
G) originates动词
from where 引导的地点从句缺谓语 + 主语 it 单三

from where it originates = 「从它发源的地方」 it simply bounces back in the opposite direction from where it __(34)__. 光被反射后沿反方向回到「它最初出发/发源的方向」——originate 表「起源、发源」与 from 搭配自然（originate from），完美对应「反弹回光线最初来的地方」。
I)permeatespermeate 强调「渗透、弥漫」，与「反弹回起点」语义不符 permeate 描述向各方向扩散浸入，无「起点 / 来处」之意；from where it permeates 既不构成习惯表达，也违背物理「光从原方向反弹回去」的描述。
B) completely副词
instead of 后接动名词 passing，空在 of 与 passing 之间作状语

completely = 「完全地」，与 instead of 形成「反射 vs 完全穿透」的对照 they reflect back out of the droplet instead of __(35)__ passing through the water. 上文说光在水滴另一侧「反射回来」，而非「完全穿过水滴」——completely 强调「彻底/全部」穿过去，与 reflect back 构成自然对比。
L)recklesslyrecklessly 含「鲁莽」感情色彩，与物理过程不符 recklessly 形容人的行为「不顾后果」，带主观贬义；光是物理对象，无所谓「鲁莽地穿过水」，逻辑荒谬。

longreading.title: 2024年6月·第3套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) Phyllis Hartman knows what it's like to make one's way through the depths of office meeting hell. Managers at one of her former human resources jobs arranged so many meetings that attendees would fall asleep at the table or intentionally arrive late. With hours of her day blocked up with unnecessary meetings, she was often forced to make up her work during overtime. "I was actually working more hours than I probably would have needed to get the work done," says Hartman, who is founder and president of PGHR Consulting in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
passages.zh: 菲利斯·哈特曼深知如何在办公室会议地狱的深处设法应对。她曾任职的一家人力资源部门的管理人员安排了如此之多的会议，以至于与会者会趴在桌边睡着，或者故意迟到。一天中有几个小时被不必要的会议占满，她常常不得不通过加班来补做工作。“实际上，我工作的时间比完成这些工作本来所需的时间还要长，”哈特曼说。她是宾夕法尼亚州匹兹堡市PGHR咨询公司的创始人兼总裁。

passages.en: B) She isn't alone in her frustration. Between 11 million and 55 million meetings are held each day in the United States, costing most organisations between 7% and 15% of their personnel budgets. Every week, employees spend about six hours in meetings, while the average manager meets for a staggering 23 hours.
passages.zh: 她并不是唯一对此感到沮丧的人。美国每天举行的会议在1100万至5500万场之间，使大多数组织的人事预算增加了7%至15%的成本。员工每周大约花6个小时参加会议，而管理者平均每周参加会议的时间竟达23小时。

passages.en: C) And though experts agree that traditional meetings are essential for making certain decisions and developing strategy, some employees view them as one of the most unnecessary parts of the workday. The result is not only hundreds of billions of wasted dollars, but an annoyance of what organisational psychologists call "meeting recovery syndrome (MRS)": time spent cooling off and regaining focus after a useless meeting. If you run to the office kitchen to get some relief with colleagues after a frustrating meeting, you're likely experiencing meeting recovery syndrome.
passages.zh: 尽管专家一致认为，传统会议对于作出某些决定和制定战略至关重要，但一些员工却把会议视为工作日中最没有必要的环节之一。其结果不仅是数千亿美元的浪费，还带来了组织心理学家所称的“会议恢复综合征”（MRS）这一烦恼：在无用的会议结束后，人们需要花时间平复情绪并重新集中注意力。如果一次令人沮丧的会议后，你跑到办公室茶水间和同事一起寻求一些慰藉，那么你很可能正在经历会议恢复综合征。

passages.en: D) Meeting recovery syndrome is a concept that should be familiar to almost anyone who has held a formal job. It isn't ground-breaking to say workers feel fatigued after a meeting, but only in recent decades have scientists deemed the condition worthy of further investigation. With its links to organisational efficiency and employee wellbeing, MRS has attracted the attention of psychologists aware of the need to understand its precise causes and cures.
passages.zh: 会议恢复综合征这一概念，几乎任何做过正式工作的人都应当有所了解。说员工在会议后会感到疲惫并不新奇，但直到最近几十年，科学家才认为这种状况值得进一步研究。由于与组织效率和员工福祉有关，会议恢复综合征吸引了心理学家的关注，他们意识到有必要了解其确切原因和应对方法。

passages.en: E) Today, in so far as researchers can hypothesise, MRS is most easily understood as a slow renewal of finite mental and physical resources. When an employee sits through an ineffective meeting their brain power is essentially being drained away. Meetings drain vitality if they last too long, fail to engage employees or turn into one-sided lectures. The conservation of resources theory, originally proposed in 1989 by Dr Stevan Hobfoll, states that psychological stress occurs when a person's resources are threatened or lost. When resources are low, a person will shift into defence to conserve their remaining supply. In the case of office meetings, where some of employees' most valuable resources are their focus, alertness and motivation, this can mean an abrupt halt in productivity as they take time to recover.
passages.zh: 如今，就研究人员能够提出的假说而言，会议恢复综合征最容易被理解为有限的脑力和体力资源缓慢恢复的过程。当员工坐着参加一场低效会议时，他们的脑力实际上正在被消耗。如果会议持续时间过长、无法调动员工参与，或演变成单方面的讲座，就会耗损他们的活力。斯特凡·霍布福尔博士于1989年最初提出的资源保存理论认为，当一个人的资源受到威胁或损失时，就会产生心理压力。当资源不足时，人会进入防御状态，以保存剩余的资源。在办公室会议中，员工最宝贵的资源包括专注力、警觉性和积极性，这种情况可能意味着生产力会突然停止，因为他们需要花时间恢复。

passages.en: F) As humans, when we transition from one task to another on the job—say from sitting in a meeting to doing normal work—it takes an effortful cognitive switch. We must detach ourselves from the previous task and expend significant mental energy to move on. If we are already drained to dangerous levels, then making the mental switch to the next thing is extra tough. It's common to see people cyber-loafing after a frustrating meeting, going and getting coffee, interrupting a colleague and telling them about the meeting, and so on.
passages.zh: 作为人类，当我们在工作中从一项任务转换到另一项任务时，比如从坐在会议中转而进行日常工作，就需要经历一个耗费努力的认知切换。我们必须从先前的任务中抽离出来，并消耗大量的脑力才能继续进行下一项任务。如果我们已经疲惫到危险的程度，那么在心理上切换到下一件事就格外困难。一次令人沮丧的会议后，人们常常会上网摸鱼、去喝咖啡、打断同事并向他们讲述会议情况，等等。

passages.en: G) Each person's ability to recover from horrible meetings is different. Some can bounce back quickly, while others carry their fatigue until the end of the workday. Yet while no formal MRS studies are currently underway, one can loosely speculate on the length of an average employee's lag time. Switching tasks in a non-MRS condition takes about 10 to 15 minutes. With MRS, it may take as long as 45 minutes on average. It's even worse when a worker has several meetings that are separated by 30 minutes. "Not enough time to transition in a non-MRS situation to get anything done, and in an MRS situation, not quite enough time to recover for the next meeting," says researcher Joseph Allen. "Then, add the compounding of back-to-back bad meetings and we may have an epidemic on our hands."
passages.zh: 每个人从糟糕会议中恢复的能力各不相同。有些人能够迅速恢复状态，而另一些人则会一直疲惫到工作日结束。然而，尽管目前还没有正式开展会议恢复综合征研究，我们仍可以大致推测普通员工的滞后时间。在非会议恢复综合征的情况下，转换任务大约需要10至15分钟。出现会议恢复综合征时，平均可能需要长达45分钟。如果一名员工参加了几场彼此间隔30分钟的会议，情况甚至会更糟。研究人员约瑟夫·艾伦说：“在没有会议恢复综合征的情况下，时间不足以完成任何事情；而在出现会议恢复综合征的情况下，时间又不足以恢复状态、准备参加下一场会议。再加上连续糟糕会议产生的叠加效应，我们可能正面临一场流行病。”

passages.en: H) In an effort to combat the side effects of MRS, Allen, along with researcher Joseph Mroz and colleagues at the University of Nebraska-Omaha, published a study detailing the best ways to avoid common traps, including a concise checklist of do's and don'ts applicable to any workplace. Drawing from around 200 papers to compile their comprehensive list, Mroz and his team may now hold a remedy to the largely undefined problem of MRS.
passages.zh: 为了应对会议恢复综合征的副作用，艾伦与研究人员约瑟夫·莫罗兹以及内布拉斯加大学奥马哈分校的同事发表了一项研究，详细说明了避免常见陷阱的最佳方法，其中包括一份适用于任何工作场所的简明“应该做”和“不应该做”清单。莫罗兹及其团队参考了约200篇论文，汇编出这份全面的清单，如今他们或许已经找到了解决会议恢复综合征这一长期缺乏明确界定的问题的方法。

passages.en: I) Mroz says a good place to start is asking ourselves if our meetings are even necessary in the first place. If all that's on the agenda is a quick catch-up, or some non-urgent information sharing, it may better suit the group to send around an email instead. "The second thing I would always recommend is keep the meeting as small as possible," says Mroz. "If they don't actually have some kind of immediate input, then they can follow up later. They don't need to be sitting in this hour-long meeting." Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to more employee engagement in the meetings they do attend, which experts agree is a proven remedy for MRS.
passages.zh: 莫罗兹说，一个好的起点是问问自己，我们的会议是否真的有必要。如果议程上的全部内容只是快速沟通近况，或分享一些不紧急的信息，那么向大家发送一封电子邮件也许更适合。“我始终建议的第二件事，是让会议规模尽可能小，”莫罗兹说。“如果他们实际上没有什么需要立即提供的意见，那么之后再跟进就可以了。他们没有必要坐在这场长达一小时的会议里。”减少参加会议的时间，最终会让员工更加投入他们确实参加的会议，而专家一致认为，提高参与度是解决会议恢复综合征的有效方法。

passages.en: J) Employees also feel taxed when they are invited together to meetings that don't inspire participation, says Cliff Scott, professor of organisational science. It takes precious time for them to vent their emotions, complain and try to regain focus after a pointless meeting—one of the main traps of MRS. Over time as employees find themselves tied up in more and more unnecessary meetings—and thus dealing with increasing lag times from MRS—the waste of workday hours can feel insulting.
passages.zh: 组织科学教授克利夫·斯科特说，当员工被召集起来参加无法激发参与感的会议时，他们也会感到精力和时间受到消耗。一次毫无意义的会议结束后，他们需要耗费宝贵的时间宣泄情绪、抱怨并努力重新集中注意力，而这正是会议恢复综合征的主要陷阱之一。随着时间推移，当员工发现自己被越来越多不必要的会议占据时间，并因此应对会议恢复综合征造成的不断增加的滞后时间时，工作日时间的浪费会让人感觉受到了侮辱。

passages.en: K) Despite the relative scarcity of research behind the subject, Hartman has taught herself many of the same tricks suggested in Mroz's study, and has come a long way since her days of being stuck with unnecessary meetings. The people she invites to meetings today include not just the essential employees, but also representatives from every department that might have a stake in the issue at hand. Managers like her, who seek input even from non-experts to shape their decisions, can find greater support and cooperation from their workforce, she says.
passages.zh: 尽管关于这一主题的研究相对匮乏，哈特曼已经自学掌握了莫罗兹研究中提出的许多相同技巧，与过去被不必要的会议困住的日子相比，她已经取得了长足进步。如今，她邀请参加会议的人不仅包括必不可少的员工，还包括所有可能与当前议题有利害关系的部门代表。她说，像她这样即使向非专家征求意见、以此来形成决策的管理者，可以从员工队伍中获得更大的支持与合作。

passages.en: L) If an organisation were to apply all 22 suggestions from Mroz and Allen's findings, the most noticeable difference would be a stark decrease in the total number of meetings on the schedule, Mroz says. Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to increased productivity, which is the ultimate objective of convening a meeting. While none of the counter-MRS ideas have been tested empirically yet, Allen says one trick with promise is for employees to identify things that quickly change their mood from negative to positive. As simple as it sounds, finding a personal happy place, going there and then coming straight back to work might be key to facilitating recovery.
passages.zh: 莫罗兹说，如果一个组织采用莫罗兹和艾伦研究结果中的全部22条建议，最明显的变化将是日程表上会议总数的大幅减少。减少会议时间最终会提高生产力，而这正是召开会议的最终目标。尽管目前还没有对这些抵抗会议恢复综合征的方法进行实证检验，艾伦说，一个有希望的技巧是让员工找出那些能迅速使自己的情绪从消极转为积极的事物。听起来很简单，但找到一个能让自己感到愉快的地方，去那里待一会儿，然后立即回到工作中，或许是促进恢复的关键。

passages.en: M) Leaders should also see themselves as "stewards of everyone else's valuable time", adds Steven Rogelberg, author of The Surprising Science of Meetings. Having the skills to foresee potential traps and treat employees' endurance with care allows leaders to provide effective short-term deterrents to MRS.
passages.zh: 《会议的惊人科学》一书的作者史蒂文·罗格尔伯格补充说，领导者还应把自己视为“其他所有人宝贵时间的守护者”。具备预见潜在陷阱的能力，并谨慎对待员工的耐受力，可以让领导者有效地在短期内遏制会议恢复综合征。

passages.en: N) Most important, however, is for organisations to awaken to the concept of meetings being flexible, says Allen. By reshaping the way they prioritise employees' time, companies can eliminate the very sources of MRS in their tracks.
passages.zh: 然而，最重要的是，组织应当意识到会议具有灵活性，艾伦说。通过重新调整对员工时间的优先安排方式，公司可以从根本上消除会议恢复综合征的来源。

statements.en: Although employees are said to be fatigued by meetings, the condition has not been considered worthy of further research until recently.
statements.zh: 尽管据说员工对会议感到疲惫,但直到最近这种状况才被认为值得进一步研究。

analysis.锚点: 近期才被认为值得深入研究
analysis.定位: D 段 It isn't ground-breaking to say workers feel fatigued after a meeting, but only in recent decades have scientists deemed the condition worthy of further investigation. 说员工开完会感到疲惫并不是什么新鲜事，但只有在最近几十年里，科学家才认为这一状况值得进一步研究。
analysis.改写: employees are said to be fatigued by meetings↔It isn't ground-breaking to say workers feel fatigued after a meeting 员工开会感到疲惫的同义改写 the condition has not been considered worthy of further research until recently↔only in recent decades have scientists deemed the condition worthy of further investigation 时间副词与同根词等值替换

statements.en: Mroz and his team compiled a list of what to do and what not to do to remedy the problem of MRS.
statements.zh: Mroz和他的团队编制了一份应该做什么和不应该做什么的清单,以解决会议恢复综合征的问题。

analysis.锚点: Mroz 团队编「该做与不该做」清单
analysis.定位: H 段 In an effort to combat the side effects of MRS, Allen, along with researcher Joseph Mroz and colleagues at the University of Nebraska-Omaha, published a study detailing the best ways to avoid common traps, including a concise checklist of do's and don'ts applicable to any workplace. 为了对抗 MRS 的副作用，Allen 与研究者 Joseph Mroz 及内布拉斯加大学奥马哈分校的同事们发表了一项研究，详述躲开常见陷阱的最佳做法，并附上一份适用于任何工作场所的「该做与不该做」简明清单。

statements.en: Companies can get rid of the root cause of MRS if they give priority to workers' time.
statements.zh: 如果公司优先考虑员工的时间,就能消除会议恢复综合征的根本原因。

analysis.锚点: 把员工时间放在优先位，根除 MRS
analysis.定位: N 段 By reshaping the way they prioritise employees' time, companies can eliminate the very sources of MRS in their tracks. 通过重塑公司对员工时间的优先排序方式，企业可以在源头就消除 MRS 的根因。
analysis.改写: get rid of the root cause of MRS↔eliminate the very sources of MRS in their tracks 动词同义加名词同义双替换 give priority to workers' time↔prioritise employees' time 动词短语与同义单词
analysis.辨邻: L the most noticeable difference would be a stark decrease in the total number of meetings on the schedule 表达的是「会议数量下降」这一可观察结果，并未涉及「根源」或「优先员工时间」，与 Q38 问的「根除」不是同一指向。 the most noticeable difference would be a stark decrease in the total number of meetings on the schedule

statements.en: If workers are exhausted to a dangerous degree, it is extremely hard for them to transition to the next task.
statements.zh: 如果员工疲惫到危险的程度,他们就极难过渡到下一项任务。

analysis.锚点: 危险疲惫程度下切换任务极其困难
analysis.定位: F 段 If we are already drained to dangerous levels, then making the mental switch to the next thing is extra tough. 如果我们已经被消耗到危险的程度，那么把心思切换到下一件事就格外吃力。
analysis.改写: If workers are exhausted to a dangerous degree↔If we are already drained to dangerous levels 条件句的同义词逐对替换 it is extremely hard for them to transition to the next task↔making the mental switch to the next thing is extra tough 形容词与动名词的同义改写
analysis.辨邻: E E 段虽强调 Meetings drain vitality 与 shift into defence，但讨论的是 Hobfoll 资源保存理论及生产力骤停的整体机制，并未承载「已经被耗到危险程度时切换格外艰难」这一具体论断。 Meetings drain vitality if they last too long, fail to engage employees or turn into one-sided lectures

statements.en: Employees in America spend a lot of time attending meetings while the number of hours managers meet is several times more.
statements.zh: 美国员工花费大量时间参加会议,而管理人员开会的小时数则是其数倍。

analysis.锚点: 美国员工开会时长与经理时长数倍对比
analysis.定位: B 段 Every week, employees spend about six hours in meetings, while the average manager meets for a staggering 23 hours. 每周，员工大约花六小时在会议上，而经理们平均开会的时长达到惊人的 23 小时。
analysis.改写: Employees in America spend a lot of time attending meetings↔Every week, employees spend about six hours in meetings 地理背景加模糊量化的同义对应 the number of hours managers meet is several times more↔the average manager meets for a staggering 23 hours 倍数关系与具体数字比较

statements.en: Phyllis Hartman has learned by herself many of the ways Mroz suggested in his study and made remarkable success in freeing herself from unnecessary meetings.
statements.zh: Phyllis Hartman自己学会了Mroz在其研究中建议的许多方法,并在使自己摆脱不必要的会议方面取得了显著成功。

analysis.锚点: Phyllis Hartman 自学 Mroz 招数
analysis.定位: K 段 Despite the relative scarcity of research behind the subject, Hartman has taught herself many of the same tricks suggested in Mroz's study, and has come a long way since her days of being stuck with unnecessary meetings. 尽管这一主题的研究相对匮乏，Hartman 还是自学了 Mroz 研究中所建议的许多招式，并且从当年被无谓会议困住的日子算起，已经取得了相当大的进步。
analysis.改写: Phyllis Hartman has learned by herself many of the ways Mroz suggested in his study↔Hartman has taught herself many of the same tricks suggested in Mroz's study 反身动词与名词同义替换 made remarkable success in freeing herself from unnecessary meetings↔has come a long way since her days of being stuck with unnecessary meetings 习语与同义解释
analysis.辨邻: A A 段虽然出现 Phyllis Hartman，但讲的是她当年在前一份人力资源工作中被会议困扰、需要 make up her work during overtime 的早期经历，并未涉及「自学 Mroz 研究中的招数」这一进步过程，故不能作答。 I was actually working more hours than I probably would have needed to get the work done

statements.en: When meetings continue too long or don't engage employees, they deplete vitality.
statements.zh: 当会议持续时间过长或无法吸引员工参与时,会议会消耗活力。

analysis.锚点: 会议太长或不能让员工投入会耗尽 vitality
analysis.定位: E 段 Meetings drain vitality if they last too long, fail to engage employees or turn into one-sided lectures. 如果会议太久、无法吸引员工参与，或变成单方面讲座，就会耗尽员工的活力。
analysis.改写: When meetings continue too long or don't engage employees↔if they last too long, fail to engage employees 条件从句各分支的同义对应 they deplete vitality↔Meetings drain vitality 罕见动词宾语搭配的同义替换

statements.zh: 当会议时间减少时,员工会更积极地参与他们确实参加的会议。

analysis.锚点: 会议时间减少，员工在所开会议中更投入
analysis.定位: I 段 Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to more employee engagement in the meetings they do attend, which experts agree is a proven remedy for MRS. 在会议上花的时间更少，最终会让员工在他们真正参加的那些会议中更投入，专家们认为这是 MRS 已被证实的解药。

analysis.改写: Some employees consider meetings one of the most dispensable parts of the workday↔some employees view them as one of the most unnecessary parts of the workday 形容词同义加整句平移

passages.en: Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common: You know them when you hear them. Sarcasm is mostly understood through tone of voice, which is used to portray the opposite of the literal words. For example, when someone says, "Well, that's exactly what I need right now," their tone can tell you it's not what they need at all.
passages.zh: 讽刺和爵士乐有一个令人意外的共同点：听到它们时，你就能辨认出来。讽刺主要通过语气来理解，语气被用来表达与字面意思相反的含义。例如，当有人说：“嗯，这正是我现在需要的东西。”他的语气可能会告诉你，那根本不是他所需要的。

passages.en: Most frequently, sarcasm highlights an irritation or is, quite simply, mean.
passages.zh: 讽刺最常见的作用是凸显恼怒，或者说得简单些，就是刻薄。

passages.en: If you want to be happier and improve your relationships, cut out sarcasm. Why? Because sarcasm is actually hostility disguised as humor.
passages.zh: 如果你想变得更快乐并改善人际关系，那就戒掉讽刺。为什么？因为讽刺实际上是伪装成幽默的敌意。

passages.en: Despite smiling outwardly, many people who receive sarcastic comments feel put down and often think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible. Indeed, it's not surprising that the origin of the word sarcasm derives from the Greek word "sarkazein" which literally means "to tear or strip the flesh off." Hence, it's no wonder that sarcasm is often preceded by the word "cutting" and that it hurts.
passages.zh: 尽管表面上带着微笑，许多听到讽刺话语的人却感到受辱，常常认为讽刺者粗鲁或令人鄙夷。事实上，sarcasm 一词源自希腊语“sarkazein”，其字面意思是“撕裂或剥去皮肉”，这并不令人意外。因此，讽刺常常被“尖刻”一词修饰，也难怪它会令人感到受伤。

passages.en: What's more, since actions strongly determine thoughts and feelings, when a person consistently acts sarcastically it may only serve to heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity. After all, when you come right down to it, sarcasm can be used as a subtle form of bullying—and most bullies are angry, insecure, or cowardly.
passages.zh: 此外，由于行为会强烈影响思想和感受，一个人如果一贯以讽刺的方式行事，可能只会加剧其潜在的敌意和不安全感。毕竟，归根结底，讽刺可以被用作一种隐蔽的欺凌形式，而大多数欺凌者都愤怒、缺乏安全感或怯懦。

passages.en: Alternatively, when a person stops voicing negative comments, especially sarcastic ones, they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident. Also, other people in their life benefit even more because they no longer have to hear the emotionally hurtful language of sarcasm.
passages.zh: 相反，当一个人不再说消极的话，尤其是不再说讽刺的话时，他们可能很快就会开始感到更加快乐，也更加自信。此外，他们生活中的其他人获益更多，因为他们不再需要听到在情感上具有伤害性的讽刺言语。

passages.en: Now, I'm not saying all sarcasm is bad. It may just be better used sparingly—like a potent spice in cooking. Too much of the spice, and the dish will be overwhelmed by it. Similarly, an occasional dash of sarcastic wit can spice up a chat and add an element of humor to it. But a big or steady serving of sarcasm will overwhelm the emotional flavor of any conversation and can taste very bitter to its recipient.
passages.zh: 我并不是说所有的讽刺都不好。或许少用一些会更好，就像烹饪中使用强烈的香料一样。香料放得太多，整道菜都会被它的味道压过。同样，偶尔来一点讽刺性的机智，可以为聊天增添情趣和幽默元素。但大剂量或持续不断的讽刺，会压过任何谈话的情感基调，让听者尝到十分苦涩的滋味。

passages.en: So, tone down the sarcasm and work on clever wit instead, which is usually without any hostility and thus more appreciated by those you're communicating with. In essence, sarcasm is easy while true, harmless wit takes talent.
passages.zh: 所以，收敛一些讽刺，转而运用巧妙的机智，因为机智通常不带有敌意，因此更容易得到交流对象的欣赏。从本质上说，讽刺很容易，而真正无害的机智则需要才华。

passages.en: Thus, the main difference between wit and sarcasm is that, as already stated, sarcasm is often hostility disguised as humor. It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting. Witty statements are usually in response to someone's unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities. Sarcastic statements are expressed in a cutting manner; witty remarks are delivered with undisguised and harmless humor.
passages.zh: 因此，机智与讽刺之间的主要区别在于，正如前文所述，讽刺常常是伪装成幽默的敌意。它可能意在伤人，而且往往尖酸刻薄、咄咄逼人。机智的话语通常是针对某人无益的言论或行为作出的回应，其目的在于通过强调其中的荒谬之处，使问题变得清楚明白并得到理顺。讽刺的话语以尖刻的方式表达；机智的评论则以不加掩饰而又无害的幽默方式呈现。

questions.stem: Why does the author say sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common?
questions.stem_zh: 作者为什么说讽刺和爵士乐有某种令人惊讶的共同点?

options.text: Both are recognized when heard.
options.zh: 两者在被听到时都能被识别出来。

options.text: Both have exactly the same tone.
options.zh: 两者有完全相同的语调。

options.text: Both mean the opposite of what they appear to.
options.zh: 两者的含义都与其表面意思相反。

options.text: Both have hidden in them an evident irritation.
options.zh: 两者都隐藏着明显的恼怒情绪。

questions.判型: Q46 用 Why does the author say... 询问作者把 sarcasm 与 jazz 类比的具体依据，不是问主旨也不是问推断。
questions.拆句: Q46 主干为 Why does the author say + 宾语从句 sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common；宾语从句里 something 是 have 的宾语，surprisingly in common 整体作 something 的后置修饰；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P1 Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common: You know them when you hear them. 讽刺和爵士乐有一个出人意料的共同点：你一听就能认出它们。

locate.en: Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common: You know them when you hear them.
locate.zh: 讽刺和爵士乐有一个出人意料的共同点：你一听就能认出它们。

option_analysis.note: Both are recognized when heard. 是 You know them when you hear them. 的标准被动同义改写，与预判完全一致。

pairs.orig: You know them when you hear them.

option_analysis.note: 原文只说"sarcasm 借 tone of voice 传达"，从未说 sarcasm 与 jazz 拥有相同语气。
原文 Sarcasm is mostly understood through tone of voice, which is used to portray the opposite of the literal words. 把"言反其意"只归于 sarcasm，与 jazz 无关。
Most frequently, sarcasm highlights an irritation 只说 sarcasm 反映 irritation，与 jazz 无关。

questions.stem: How do many people feel when they hear sarcastic comments?
questions.stem_zh: 许多人在听到讽刺性评论时有什么感受?

options.text: They feel hostile towards the sarcastic person.
options.zh: 他们对讽刺者感到敌意。

options.text: They feel belittled and disrespected.
options.zh: 他们感到被贬低和不被尊重。

options.text: They feel a strong urge to retaliate.
options.zh: 他们感到强烈的报复冲动。

options.text: They feel incapable of disguising their irritation.
options.zh: 他们感到无法掩饰自己的恼怒。

questions.判型: Q47 用 How do many people feel 直接问感受类细节，答案应是原文情绪句的同义改写。
questions.拆句: Q47 How 引导特殊疑问，主干 do many people feel，when 引导状语从句 they hear sarcastic comments；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P4 Despite smiling outwardly, many people who receive sarcastic comments feel put down and often think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible. 尽管表面带笑，许多人在听到讽刺的话时仍会感觉被贬低，并常常认为讽刺他们的人粗鲁或可鄙。

locate.en: Despite smiling outwardly, many people who receive sarcastic comments feel put down and often think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible.
locate.zh: 尽管表面带笑，许多人在听到讽刺的话时仍会感觉被贬低，并常常认为讽刺他们的人粗鲁或可鄙。

They feel belittled and disrespected. 恰是 feel put down 的双词同义改写，与预判一致。

questions.stem: What happens when a person consistently acts sarcastically?
questions.stem_zh: 当一个人持续以讽刺方式行事时会发生什么?

options.text: They feel their dignity greatly heightened.
options.zh: 他们感到自己的尊严大大提高。

options.text: They feel increasingly insecure and hostile.
options.zh: 他们感到越来越不安全和充满敌意。

options.text: They endure hostility under the disguise of humor.
options.zh: 他们在幽默的伪装下忍受敌意。

options.text: They taste bitterness even in pleasant interactions.
options.zh: 他们即使在愉快的互动中也感到苦涩。

questions.判型: Q48 问"当某人持续讽刺时会发生什么"，是原文一个具体因果陈述，属细节题。
questions.拆句: Q48 What happens 主干 + when a person consistently acts sarcastically 时间状语从句；副词 consistently 修饰 acts，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P5 when a person consistently acts sarcastically it may only serve to heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity. 当一个人一贯地讽刺人，这种行为只会加深他内心潜藏的敌意与不安全感。

locate.en: when a person consistently acts sarcastically it may only serve to heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity.
locate.zh: 当一个人一贯地讽刺人，这种行为只会加深他内心潜藏的敌意与不安全感。

option_analysis.note: 原文加深的是 hostility/insecurity 等负面情绪，而非 dignity（尊严）；正相反，长期讽刺者被视为隐性霸凌者，尊严下滑。
They feel increasingly insecure and hostile. 把"程度加深"用 increasingly 还原，把名词敌意/不安全感转回形容词，恰是预判同义。

pairs.orig: heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity
pairs.opt: They feel increasingly insecure and hostile.

option_analysis.note: 原文 hostility disguised as humor 的施事是讽刺者本人；这里把"在 humor 伪装下被迫忍受 hostility"按到讽刺者身上，搞反了角色。
原文 can taste very bitter to its recipient 的 bitter 是接收者的感觉，且语境是"过量讽刺"，从未说"持续讽刺者在愉快互动中也尝苦"。

questions.stem: What does the author say about people quitting sarcastic comments?
questions.stem_zh: 作者对人们停止讽刺性评论有何看法?

options.text: It makes others happier and more self-confident.
options.zh: 这让其他人更快乐、更自信。

options.text: It restrains them from being irritating and bullying.
options.zh: 这约束他们不再恼人和欺凌。

options.text: It benefits not only themselves but also those around them.
options.zh: 这不仅有益于他们自己,也有益于周围的人。

options.text: It shields them from negative comments and outright hostility.
options.zh: 这使他们免受负面评论和公然敌意的影响。

questions.判型: Q49 用 What does the author say about... 询问作者对"停讽"的具体陈述，属对应一句原文的细节题。
questions.拆句: Q49 主干 What does the author say + about 介词短语；about 的宾语是动名词短语 people quitting sarcastic comments；结构无陷阱。
questions.定位: P6 Alternatively, when a person stops voicing negative comments, especially sarcastic ones, they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident. Also, other people in their life benefit even more because they no longer have to hear the emotionally hurtful language of sarcasm. 反过来说，当一个人不再说讽刺等负面话语时，他自己很快会更快乐、更自信；而且，他生活中的其他人受益更多，因为他们再也不必听到讽刺这种伤人的话。

locate.en: Alternatively, when a person stops voicing negative comments, especially sarcastic ones, they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident. Also, other people in their life benefit even more because they no longer have to hear the emotionally hurtful language of sarcasm.
locate.zh: 反过来说，当一个人不再说讽刺等负面话语时，他自己很快会更快乐、更自信；而且，他生活中的其他人受益更多，因为他们再也不必听到讽刺这种伤人的话。

option_analysis.note: 原文 happier and more self-confident 的主语是讽刺者本人，A 只说让 others 更乐更自信，丢掉了"自己"那一半。
原文虽在 can be used as a subtle form of bullying 提及 bullying，但 P6 描述停讽效果时根本没出现"约束自己别再霸凌"的说法。
It benefits not only themselves but also those around them. 用 not only...but also 同时呼应 may soon start to feel happier 与 other people in their life benefit even more，与预判一致。

pairs.orig: they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident
other people in their life benefit even more

option_analysis.note: 原文是"停讽者不再向外发讽刺、让他人不必听到"，并非"屏蔽讽刺者本人免受外界负面话语"，方向相反。

questions.stem: What is the chief difference between a speaker's wit and sarcasm?
questions.stem_zh: 说话者的机智和讽刺之间的主要区别是什么?

options.text: Their appreciation.
options.zh: 它们的欣赏程度。

options.text: Their emphasis.
options.zh: 它们的侧重点。

options.text: Their intention.
options.zh: 它们的意图。

questions.拆句: Q50 主干 What is the chief difference + 后置介词短语 between a speaker's wit and sarcasm；between 引导比较对象；结构无陷阱。
questions.定位: P9 Thus, the main difference between wit and sarcasm is that, as already stated, sarcasm is often hostility disguised as humor. It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting. Witty statements are usually in response to someone's unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities. 于是，机智与讽刺的主要区别在于：讽刺常是"敌意伪装成幽默"，可能意在伤人；而机智之语意在厘清问题、点出其荒谬之处。

locate.en: Thus, the main difference between wit and sarcasm is that, as already stated, sarcasm is often hostility disguised as humor. It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting. Witty statements are usually in response to someone's unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities.
locate.zh: 于是，机智与讽刺的主要区别在于：讽刺常是"敌意伪装成幽默"，可能意在伤人；而机智之语意在厘清问题、点出其荒谬之处。

option_analysis.note: untangle and clarify the issue 只出现在 wit 一侧；讽刺侧从未谈到 clarity 这一维度。
原文 more appreciated by those you're communicating with 谈的是"听者是否欣赏"，是结果而非区别本身。
by emphasizing its absurdities 中 emphasizing 仅是 wit 实现意图的手段，不是对比双方共有的维度。
Their intention. 把原文 sarcasm 的 be intended to hurt 与 wit 的 intent is to untangle and clarify 抽象为共同维度 intention，与预判一致。

the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue

reading2.title: 2024年6月·第3套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: Variability is crucially important for learning new skills. Consider learning how to serve in tennis. Should you always practise serving from the exactly same location on the court, aiming at the same spot? Although practising in more variable conditions will be slower at first, it will likely make you a better tennis player in the end. This is because variability leads to better generalisation of what is learned.
passages.zh: 可变性对于学习新技能至关重要。以学习如何在网球比赛中发球为例。你是否应该总是在球场上完全相同的位置练习发球，并瞄准同一个点？虽然在更加多变的条件下练习起初会比较慢，但最终很可能会使你成为更优秀的网球运动员。这是因为可变性会使所学内容得到更好的泛化。

passages.en: This principle is found in many domains, including speech perception and learning categories. For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category "dog" if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.
passages.zh: 这一原则存在于许多领域，包括语音感知和类别学习。例如，如果婴儿接触到的只有吉娃娃，而不是许多不同种类的狗，那么他们将很难学会“狗”这一类别。

passages.en: "There are over ten different names for this basic principle," says Limor Raviv, the senior investigator of a recent study. "Learning from less variable input is often fast, but may fail to generalise to new stimuli."
passages.zh: 最近一项研究的高级研究员利莫尔·拉维夫说：“这一基本原则有十多个不同的名称。根据可变性较小的输入进行学习通常速度较快，但可能无法泛化到新的刺激上。”

passages.en: To identify key patterns and understand the underlying principles of variability effects, Raviv and her colleagues reviewed over 150 studies on variability and generalisation across fields, including computer science, linguistics, categorisation, visual perception and formal education.
passages.zh: 为了确定关键模式并理解可变性效应背后的基本原则，拉维夫和她的同事们对来自计算机科学、语言学、分类、视觉感知和正规教育等领域的150多项有关可变性和泛化的研究进行了综述。

passages.en: The researchers discovered that, across studies, the term variability can refer to at least four different kinds of variability, such as set size and scheduling. "These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv.
passages.zh: 研究人员发现，在不同的研究中，“可变性”一词至少可以指四种不同类型的可变性，例如集合大小和安排方式。拉维夫说：“这四种可变性从未被直接比较过，这意味着我们目前还不知道哪一种对学习最有效。”

passages.en: The impact of variability depends on whether it is relevant to the task or not. But according to the 'Mr. Miyagi principle', practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills.
passages.zh: 可变性的影响取决于它是否与任务相关。但根据“宫城先生原则”，练习看似无关的技能实际上可能有益于其他技能的学习。

passages.en: But why does variability impact learning and generalisation? One theory is that more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not.
passages.zh: 但是，为什么可变性会影响学习和泛化呢？一种理论认为，可变性更大的输入能够凸显任务中哪些方面是相关的，哪些方面则不相关。

passages.en: Another theory is that greater variability leads to broader generalisations. This is because variability will represent the real world better, including atypical(非典型的) examples.
passages.zh: 另一种理论认为，更大的可变性会带来更广泛的泛化。这是因为可变性能够更好地呈现现实世界，包括非典型的例子。

passages.en: A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.
passages.zh: 第三个原因与记忆的运作方式有关：当训练具有可变性时，学习者会被迫主动重建自己的记忆。

passages.en: "Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life. Beyond affecting the way we learn language, motor skills, and categories, it even has an impact on our social lives," explains Raviv. "For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community. Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory."
passages.zh: 拉维夫解释说：“了解可变性的影响对于我们日常生活的每一个方面都确实很重要。除了影响我们学习语言、运动技能和类别的方式之外，它甚至还会影响我们的社交生活。例如，人脸识别会受到人们是在小型社区还是较大社区中长大的影响。童年时期接触较少的人脸与面孔记忆能力减弱有关。”

passages.en: "We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv. "Our paper raises a lot of open questions. Can we find similar effects of variability beyond the brain, for instance, in the immune system?"
passages.zh: 拉维夫总结道：“我们希望这项工作能够激发人们的好奇心，并推动开展更多有关这一主题的研究。我们的论文提出了许多尚未解决的问题。我们能否在大脑之外发现类似的可变性效应，例如在免疫系统中？”

questions.stem: What does the passage say about infants learning the category "dog" if they are exposed to Chihuahuas only?
questions.stem_zh: 如果婴儿只接触吉娃娃,文章对婴儿学习"狗"这一类别有何说法?

options.text: They will encounter some degree of difficulty.
options.zh: 他们会遇到一定程度的困难。

options.text: They will try to categorise other objects first.
options.zh: 他们会先尝试对其他物体进行分类。

options.text: They will prefer Chihuahuas to other dog species.
options.zh: 他们会更喜欢吉娃娃而非其他犬种。

options.text: They will imagine Chihuahuas in various conditions.
options.zh: 他们会想象吉娃娃在各种情况下的样子。

questions.判型: What does the passage say about infants learning the category "dog" if they are exposed to Chihuahuas only? 以 What does the passage say about... 起手，要求复述原文事实，没有 infer/suggest 等推断信号。
questions.拆句: Q51 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 What does the passage say about infants learning the category "dog"，其中 learning the category "dog" 是 v-ing 短语做 infants 的后置定语；末尾 if they are exposed to Chihuahuas only 是条件状语从句，被动语态 are exposed to 意为“只接触到”，是理解前提。
questions.定位: P2 For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category "dog" if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs. 举例来说，如果婴儿只接触吉娃娃，而不是接触多种不同种类的狗，他们将很难学会“狗”这一类别。

locate.en: For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category "dog" if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.
locate.zh: 举例来说，如果婴儿只接触吉娃娃，而不是接触多种不同种类的狗，他们将很难学会“狗”这一类别。

option_analysis.note: 预判“会有学习困难”与 encounter some degree of difficulty 在语义上严格对应，无需推断，直接锁定 A。
They will try to categorise other objects first 在 P2 找不到任何对应——原文只说他们 struggle to learn“狗”，未说他们会先去分类别的东西。
They will prefer Chihuahuas to other dog species 把原文“只接触到吉娃娃”曲解为“偏好吉娃娃”——原文谈的是输入受限导致学习困难，与个人偏好无关。
They will imagine Chihuahuas in various conditions 把第 1 段“在多变条件下练习”的概念硬塞到婴儿身上——原文中婴儿并不会主动 imagine，“in various conditions”是上一段网球训练的语境。

questions.stem: What does Raviv say about the four different kinds of variability?
questions.stem_zh: Raviv对四种不同类型的变异性有何说法?

options.text: Which of them is most relevant to the task at hand is to be confirmed.
options.zh: 其中哪一种与手头的任务最相关有待确认。

options.text: Why they have an impact on learning is far from being understood.
options.zh: 它们为何对学习产生影响远未被理解。

options.text: Why they have never been directly compared remains a mystery.
options.zh: 它们为何从未被直接比较过仍是一个谜。

options.text: Which of them is most conducive to learning is yet to be identified.
options.zh: 其中哪一种最有利于学习尚待确定。

questions.判型: What does Raviv say about the four different kinds of variability? 用 say about 句式问 Raviv 对四种 variability 的明确表述，是事实复述而非推断。
questions.拆句: Q52 主干 What does Raviv say，介词短语 about the four different kinds of variability 限定话题范围；句中 the four different kinds of 含定冠词 the，提示原文已先有这“四种”的提及。
questions.定位: P5 "These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv. Raviv 说：“这四种 variability 从未被直接比较过——这意味着我们目前还不知道哪种对学习最有效。”

locate.en: "These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv.
locate.zh: Raviv 说：“这四种 variability 从未被直接比较过——这意味着我们目前还不知道哪种对学习最有效。”

option_analysis.note: Which of them is most relevant to the task at hand is to be confirmed 把原文的 most effective for learning（对学习最有效）偷换为 most relevant to the task at hand（对手头任务最相关）——relevant to the task 是第 6 段的话题，不是第 5 段 Raviv 引语的内容。
Why they have an impact on learning is far from being understood 是关于“机制为何”的论断，不是 Raviv 在第 5 段就四种 variability 所说的话；况且第 7–9 段恰恰给出了三种 theory，“远未被理解”与原文也不符。
Why they have never been directly compared remains a mystery 把原文 These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared 的事实（“未被比较”）扭曲成“为何未被比较仍是谜”——原文从未说“为何未被比较”是个谜。
无论是“目前不知→尚待确认”的含蓄否定，还是“最有效→最有助益”的形容词替换，都精准落在 D 项措辞上，锁定 D。

pairs.orig: we currently don't know which is most effective for learning
pairs.opt: Which of them is most conducive to learning is yet to be identified

questions.stem: How does one of the theories explain the importance of variability for learning new skills?
questions.stem_zh: 其中一种理论如何解释变异性对学习新技能的重要性?

options.text: Learners regard variable training as typical of what happens in the real world.
options.zh: 学习者认为变化训练是现实世界中发生情况的典型代表。

options.text: Learners receiving variable training are compelled to reorganise their memories.
options.zh: 接受变化训练的学习者被迫重组其记忆。

options.text: Learners pay attention to the relevant aspects of a task and ignore those irrelevant.
options.zh: 学习者关注任务的相关方面并忽略不相关的方面。

options.text: Learners focus on related skills instead of wasting time and effort on unrelated ones.
options.zh: 学习者专注于相关技能而不是在不相关技能上浪费时间和精力。

questions.判型: How does one of the theories explain the importance of variability for learning new skills? 问“某个理论怎么解释”，要求复述原文中三个理论之一的具体内容，仍属细节题。
questions.拆句: Q53 How 引导特殊疑问，主干 How does one of the theories explain the importance，of 短语 of variability for learning new skills 限定 importance，并不影响理解。注意 one of the theories 用单数动词 explain，提示只问其中一个理论。
questions.定位: P9 A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories. 第三个原因与记忆的运作方式有关：当训练具有多变性时，学习者被迫主动地重构他们的记忆。

locate.en: A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.
locate.zh: 第三个原因与记忆的运作方式有关：当训练具有多变性时，学习者被迫主动地重构他们的记忆。

option_analysis.note: Learners regard variable training as typical of what happens in the real world 把 variability will represent the real world better, including atypical examples 颠倒——原文是“多变训练能更好地代表真实世界（包含非典型例子）”，并非“学习者把多变训练视为典型”。
条件状语从句→v-ing 定语、被动词组→被动词组、动词短语→动词短语三层替换齐全，正确项 B 与定位句构成一对一映射。

pairs.opt: Learners receiving variable training are compelled to reorganise their memories

option_analysis.note: Learners pay attention to the relevant aspects of a task and ignore those irrelevant 把 more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not 偷换主语——原文是“多变输入会突显相关/不相关方面”，并非“学习者主动关注/忽略”。

Learners focus on related skills instead of wasting time and effort on unrelated ones 把 practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills 的意思颠倒——原文是“练习看似无关的技能也能助益”，选项却说“专注相关技能而不浪费在无关技能上”，恰恰相反。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about face recognition?
questions.stem_zh: 文章对面孔识别有何说法?

options.text: People growing up in a small community may find it easy to remember familiar faces.
options.zh: 在小社区长大的人可能会发现记住熟悉面孔很容易。

options.text: Face recognition has a significant impact on literally every aspect of our social lives.
options.zh: 面孔识别对我们社会生活的几乎每个方面都有重大影响。

options.text: People growing up in a large community can readily recognise any individual faces.
options.zh: 在大社区长大的人能够轻易识别任何个体面孔。

options.zh: 人们成长所在社区的规模影响其面孔识别能力。

questions.判型: What does the passage say about face recognition? 仍是 What does the passage say about 句式，问原文如何陈述 face recognition 这一事实。
questions.拆句: Q54 结构与第 51 题同款，主干 What does the passage say about face recognition? 无从句无否定，平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P10 For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community. 例如，面孔识别会受到人们是在小社区还是大社区长大这一因素的影响。

locate.en: For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community.
locate.zh: 例如，面孔识别会受到人们是在小社区还是大社区长大这一因素的影响。

option_analysis.note: People growing up in a small community may find it easy to remember familiar faces 给“小社区”贴上“易记熟人脸”的标签，但 Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory 恰恰说“接触少→记忆减弱”，与 A 的方向相反；且原文没区分 familiar faces。

Face recognition has a significant impact on literally every aspect of our social lives 把“variability 影响每一方面”安到 face recognition 头上——原文 Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life 的主语是 variability，不是 face recognition。
People growing up in a large community can readily recognise any individual faces 用 any individual faces 把原文中性的“识别能力受影响”夸大为“能轻松识别任何个人面孔”，是绝对化推断。
D 既保留了“社区规模→识别能力”的因果，也保留了“人群”层面的中性陈述，没有像 A/C 那样把因果方向具体化、特例化，最贴近原文。

pairs.opt: The size of the community people grow up in impacts their face recognition ability

questions.stem_zh: Raviv希望通过其研究工作做什么?

questions.定位: P11 "We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv. Raviv 总结说：“我们希望这项工作能激发人们的好奇心，并产生更多关于这一主题的研究。”

locate.en: "We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv.
locate.zh: Raviv 总结说：“我们希望这项工作能激发人们的好奇心，并产生更多关于这一主题的研究。”

Use the principle of variability in teaching seemingly unrelated skills in education 取自 practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills 的 Mr. Miyagi 原则，也并非 Raviv 末段表达的愿景。
C 把原文两个并列愿望 spark...curiosity 与 generate...work 都同义改写并对齐，没有遗漏其中任何一个，符合“并列动作全保留”原则。

pairs.opt: stimulate more research on the topic

translation.title: 2024年6月·第3套英语六级汉译英（段落翻译） · 介绍中国扇子的文化与艺术价值 参考译文与解析
translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 扇子自古以来就深受中国人喜爱，但现在已不只是消暑纳凉的工具，而更多地作为艺术品供人欣赏。许多扇子造型优美、做工精良，并绘有山水、花鸟、人物等精美图案，具有很高的艺术价值。中国许多著名画家和书法家喜欢在扇子上作诗绘画，展示其艺术品味。扇子常作为礼物赠予他人，表达美好的祝福和真挚的情感。如今，扇子的实用功能已大为减弱， 但作为一种文化符号和艺术形式，扇子仍然在中国传统文化中扮演着重要角色。
translation.reference_en:
Fans have long been cherished by the Chinese people. Today, however, they are no longer merely tools for keeping cool, but are more often appreciated as works of art. Many fans, with graceful shapes and exquisite workmanship, are decorated with delicate patterns of landscapes, flowers and birds, and figures, and thus carry high artistic value. In addition, many famous Chinese painters and calligraphers like to write poems and paint pictures on fans to display their artistic taste. Fans are also often given to others as gifts to convey good wishes and sincere feelings. Today, although the practical function of fans has greatly weakened, the fan, as a cultural symbol and an art form, still plays an important role in traditional Chinese culture.
【衔接】
第1句内部：补 however 显「但」但现在已不只是消暑纳凉的工具 的「但」是从「自古受喜爱」到「如今地位变化」的转折，定稿在 Today 后补 however，让转折显性化：Today, however, it is no longer merely a tool…
第1句与后文：用 it / they 承接「扇子」避免重复全篇主语都是扇子，若每句都写 the fan / fans 会重复刺眼。第1句后半已用 it 承接 扇子，行文中相邻句可灵活用 it / they 代替，减少 the fan 的机械重复。
第2、3句之间：补 In addition 体现递进第2句讲扇子本身有艺术价值，第3句讲名家在扇上题诗作画，是补充递进。可在第3句句首加 In addition / Moreover，让「不仅扇子本身美，名家还在上面创作」的层层加码显出来。
第5句承上：用 Today 标记时间转换并收束如今 标志全篇从「扇子的种种价值」转向「当下总评」，定稿保留 Today 置于句首，作为收尾段的时间标记，让结论句与前文自然分隔、形成总结。

cohesion.core: 第1句内部：补 however 显「但」
cohesion.detail: 但现在已不只是消暑纳凉的工具 的「但」是从「自古受喜爱」到「如今地位变化」的转折，定稿在 Today 后补 however，让转折显性化：Today, however, it is no longer merely a tool…

cohesion.core: 第1句与后文：用 it / they 承接「扇子」避免重复
cohesion.detail: 全篇主语都是扇子，若每句都写 the fan / fans 会重复刺眼。第1句后半已用 it 承接 扇子，行文中相邻句可灵活用 it / they 代替，减少 the fan 的机械重复。

cohesion.core: 第2、3句之间：补 In addition 体现递进
cohesion.detail: 第2句讲扇子本身有艺术价值，第3句讲名家在扇上题诗作画，是补充递进。可在第3句句首加 In addition / Moreover，让「不仅扇子本身美，名家还在上面创作」的层层加码显出来。

cohesion.core: 第5句承上：用 Today 标记时间转换并收束
cohesion.detail: 如今 标志全篇从「扇子的种种价值」转向「当下总评」，定稿保留 Today 置于句首，作为收尾段的时间标记，让结论句与前文自然分隔、形成总结。

main_idea.core: 介绍中国扇子的文化与艺术价值
main_idea.detail: 全段在客观介绍「扇子」这一中国传统物件：从它自古受喜爱，到如今由实用工具转为艺术品、文化符号。开篇 扇子自古以来就深受中国人喜爱 和结尾 扇子仍然在中国传统文化中扮演着重要角色 都是对一类事物特征与现状的客观陈述，属于典型的「中国文化介绍」语体，用词宜平实正式、不带主观情绪。

tense.detail: 全篇是对扇子「现状与普遍特征」的客观陈述（受喜爱、作为艺术品、有艺术价值、扮演重要角色），不是讲某段历史故事，故主时态用一般现在时。只有 扇子的实用功能已大为减弱 这种「已经发生并延续至今」的变化，才偏离基调改用现在完成时。

term_notes.detail: 扇子 全篇反复出现，统一译为 the fan（泛指作为一类物件时用 the fan 或复数 fans）。这是全篇主语，务必前后一致，不要一会儿 fan、一会儿 the fan、一会儿 fans 乱换。
消暑纳凉的工具 是文化负载短语，不必逐字直译「暑」「凉」，意译为 a tool for keeping cool / cooling oneself 即可，抓住「让人凉快」这一核心功能。
山水、花鸟、人物 为中国画三大传统题材，统一意译为 landscapes, flowers and birds, and figures，全篇出现一次，定此译法即可。
书法家 是文化负载词，统一译为 calligraphers，对应前面的 painters（画家），不要误译成 writers。
文化符号 统一译为 a cultural symbol，是结尾点题的关键词，定法后照用。

steps.text: 扇子被中国人喜爱 / 扇子作艺术品被欣赏（主语策略：转被动）中文 扇子自古以来就深受中国人喜爱 里「深受…喜爱」本身就是被动含义，承受者「扇子」自然作主语：The fan has been loved/cherished by the Chinese。后半 而更多地作为艺术品供人欣赏 仍以扇子为主语续写：it is now appreciated more as a work of art。主谓是 The fan — has been loved / is appreciated。

三层意思用「转折+对比」串成一句本句有三层：①自古受喜爱 ②但现在不只是工具 ③而更多作艺术品被欣赏。②③是转折后的对比，用「not just… but more as…」结构降级安放：no longer merely a tool for keeping cool, but more often appreciated as a work of art。已不只是消暑纳凉的工具 里「不只是」是关键的对比信号词，必须用 no longer merely / not just 显化。「供人欣赏」不必另起句，并进 appreciated 即可。

时态「自古以来就深受喜爱」是从过去延续到现在的状态，偏离全篇一般现在时的基调，用现在完成时 has long been loved；后半「现在…作为艺术品」是当下事实，用一般现在时 is now appreciated。两个时态在一句里各司其职。 单复数与冠词泛指扇子这一类物，可用 The fan（定冠词+单数表类指）或 Fans（复数表类指），全篇统一选一种。本篇用 The fan。 介词搭配「作为艺术品」用 as a work of art；「消暑」用 for keeping cool（for + 动名词表用途），不要写成 for keep cool。
The fan has long been cherished by the Chinese people. Today, however, it is no longer merely a tool for keeping cool, but is more often appreciated as a work of art.
许多扇子 具有 很高的艺术价值（主语策略：原句主语）中文主语明确就是 许多扇子（Many fans）。四个并列描述里，具有很高的艺术价值 是结论性的核心，可作主干谓语：Many fans are of high artistic value（或 have great artistic value）。其余三项（造型优美、做工精良、绘有图案）降级作修饰。

三条描述降级为 with 短语 + 分词「造型优美、做工精良」是名词性特征，用 with 介词短语挂上：with graceful shapes and exquisite workmanship；并绘有山水、花鸟、人物等精美图案 是被动含义，用过去分词作定语 decorated/painted with exquisite patterns of landscapes, flowers and birds, and figures。避免照中文用 and 把四个谓语平铺成 are beautiful and are well-made and are painted… 的流水句。

时态回指全篇基调，客观陈述扇子特征，用一般现在时 are / have。 主谓一致与单复数主语 Many fans 是复数，谓语用 are（不是 is）；patterns、shapes、landscapes、figures 等可数名词都用复数表泛指多样。 用词搭配「做工精良」用 exquisite workmanship（workmanship 不可数，不加 s）；「艺术价值」用 artistic value；「精美图案」用 exquisite/delicate patterns。
Many fans, with graceful shapes and exquisite workmanship, are decorated with delicate patterns of landscapes, flowers and birds, and figures, and thus carry high artistic value.

画家和书法家 喜欢 在扇子上作诗绘画（主语策略：原句主语）主语明确：中国许多著名画家和书法家（Many famous Chinese painters and calligraphers）。核心谓语是「喜欢（做某事）」：like to write poems and paint。主谓宾为 painters and calligraphers — like — to write and paint on fans。
「展示品味」降级为目的状语展示其艺术品味 不是与「作诗绘画」并列的第二个动作，而是其目的/结果，降级为非谓语 to display their artistic taste（不定式表目的）或 displaying…（现在分词表伴随结果），挂在主干后。不要写成 like to write poems and paint and display…的并列平铺。
时态回指全篇基调，陈述一种普遍偏好，用一般现在时 like。 主谓一致主语 painters and calligraphers 为复数，谓语用 like（原形复数），不用 likes。 介词与单复数「在扇子上」用 on fans（泛指多把扇子，用复数）；「作诗」write poems（诗不止一首，用复数）。
Many famous Chinese painters and calligraphers like to write poems and paint pictures on fans to display their artistic taste.
扇子 常被 作为礼物 赠予他人（主语策略：转被动）中文 扇子常作为礼物赠予他人 是无明确施动者的「赠予」动作，承受者「扇子」作主语、用被动最自然：Fans are often given as gifts。主谓为 Fans — are given。
「表达祝福情感」降级为目的状语表达美好的祝福和真挚的情感 是赠扇的目的，用不定式 to express/convey good wishes and sincere feelings 降级挂在主干后，而非另起一个并列谓语。

时态与语态陈述普遍习俗，用一般现在时被动 are given；「常」用频度副词 often 置于 are 之后。 单复数Fans 复数表类指；gifts、good wishes、sincere feelings 均用复数表泛指多种。 用词搭配「赠予他人」as gifts (to others/people)；「美好的祝福」good wishes；「真挚的情感」sincere/heartfelt feelings/emotions。
Fans are often given to others as gifts to convey good wishes and sincere feelings.

扇子 仍 扮演着 重要角色（主语策略：原句主语）本句两个分句各有主语：前句 扇子的实用功能已大为减弱 主语是「实用功能」（the practical function has weakened）；后句 扇子仍然在中国传统文化中扮演着重要角色 主语是「扇子」（the fan still plays an important role）。后句是全段落点，主谓为 the fan — plays — an important role。
用Although/but显化转折，作为短语降级前后是「功能减弱 vs 仍重要」的让步转折，用 Although… 或 …, but… 框住。作为一种文化符号和艺术形式 是后句主语扇子的身份说明，降级为介词短语 as a cultural symbol and an art form 作状语前置，不另起句。

时态「实用功能已大为减弱」是已完成并延续到现在的变化，偏离基调用现在完成时 has greatly weakened / has been greatly reduced；后句「仍然扮演着重要角色」是当下持续事实，回到一般现在时 still plays。 冠词与单复数「一种文化符号」a cultural symbol（单数加 a）、「一种艺术形式」an art form（元音前用 an）、「一个重要角色」an important role；「中国传统文化」traditional Chinese culture（culture 此处不可数、不加冠词）。 连词不并用用了 although 就不再用 but（中文「虽然…但…」并用，英文 although 和 but 只能留一个），否则语法错误。
Today, although the practical function of fans has greatly weakened, the fan, as a cultural symbol and an art form, still plays an important role in traditional Chinese culture.
